title: $120,000 Robot Hand Teardown: Who Makes the Motors, Sensors and Bearings
content:
Shadow Robot's research-grade dexterous hand costs about $120,000 (roughly ₩170 million) per unit — and it can catch a falling egg without cracking it. We opened up the reconstruction to map its key parts to the companies that make this category of component. One heads-up before the table: none of these makers are confirmed suppliers to Shadow Robot specifically — they're the representative company for each part category, which is why we write "makes this part," not "confirmed supplier."

Inside a $120,000 robot hand: four parts

PartJobRepresentative makerEvidence
20 precision DC motorsWind and pull tendon cables to move each jointMaxon (Switzerland)Not publicly traded
40 tendon strandsHigh-strength fiber cables that transmit motor force to the fingertipsSolstice Advanced Materials (NASDAQ: SOLS)Estimated: category maker of Spectra-type fiber
Fingertip tactile sensor arrayDetects grip force and contact across a fingerprint-like sensor gridMelexis (Euronext Brussels: MLXS)Estimated: category maker of precision sensor chips
Precision joint bearingsLets finger joints rotate smoothly under loadMinebea Mitsumi (TYO: 6479)Estimated: category maker of miniature bearings

Read this before the table: the manufacturer, Shadow Robot (UK), and the motor maker its own promotional material points to, Maxon (Switzerland), are both private companies. The three other names above are publicly listed companies we identified as representative makers of that part category — not confirmed Shadow Robot suppliers. We found no supplier disclosure naming any of the three for this specific product.

1. 20 precision DC motors — tendon-driven, not direct-drive

Like a human hand, this robot hand moves its fingers by winding cables rather than putting a motor in every joint: 20 precision DC motors sit in the forearm and wind tendon cables to bend each joint. Maxon, a Swiss precision motor maker used across medical devices, aerospace and robotics, is not publicly traded, so there's no stock tied to this specific component.

2. 40 tendon strands — Solstice Advanced Materials

The cables that carry motor force to the fingertips need to be thin, strong and low-stretch. Solstice Advanced Materials, listed on Nasdaq, is a representative maker of this class of high-strength synthetic fiber (Spectra-type material).

3. Fingertip tactile sensor array — Melexis

A grid of sensors packed into the fingertip, arranged like a fingerprint, detects grip force and contact. Melexis, a Belgian chipmaker listed on Euronext Brussels, is a representative maker of this kind of precision sensor chip.

4. Precision joint bearings — Minebea Mitsumi

Smooth, low-friction joint rotation under repeated load requires miniature precision bearings. Minebea Mitsumi, listed in Tokyo, is a representative maker of this bearing category.

Why it can catch a falling egg without breaking it

A typical industrial gripper just clamps down. This hand pairs a human-like tendon-driven joint structure with fingertip tactile sensing, which lets it modulate grip force in real time — the combination that makes catching a falling egg without cracking it possible.

Quick FAQ

Do these companies actually supply Shadow Robot?
Not confirmed. The three listed companies above are representative makers of each part category; we found no supplier disclosure linking any of them to this specific product. This video is a reconstruction, not a physical teardown.

Which of these companies can I actually invest in?
Solstice Advanced Materials (NASDAQ: SOLS), Melexis (Euronext Brussels: MLXS) and Minebea Mitsumi (TYO: 6479) are publicly listed. Maxon, the motor maker, is privately held.

Is this a real product?
Yes. Shadow Robot publicly lists a price of €110,000 for its research-grade dexterous hand, including delivery, installation and training.

Summary

  • 20 precision DC motors: Maxon (Switzerland) — not publicly traded
  • 40 tendon strands: Solstice Advanced Materials (NASDAQ: SOLS)
  • Fingertip tactile sensor array: Melexis (Euronext Brussels: MLXS)
  • Precision joint bearings: Minebea Mitsumi (TYO: 6479)

Sources: Shadow Robot's published pricing and product specifications; company profiles for Solstice Advanced Materials, Melexis and Minebea Mitsumi.
